specs.gpu_note: Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB (GV100GL, reported as 'Tesla PG500-216'), sm_70 Volta, 72 SM, SM clock max 1380 MHz, 32768 MiB HBM2 4096-bit @ 1107 MHz, ECC ON, 250 W cap. Measured 964.8 GB/s of 1133.6 GB/s theoretical (85%, saxpy). PCIe Gen3 x16, no downtraining. Terminal software window: driver 580.178.04 is the LAST branch supporting Volta and CUDA 12.9 is the LAST toolkit that can target sm_70 - both pinned, NVIDIA apt repo deliberately absent.
specs.ram_note: 14x8GB DDR4-2666 single-rank RDIMM at 2400 MT/s (Broadwell-EP IMC ceiling), 7 per socket so one channel per socket is half-filled (a stick failed; symmetry preferred over channel balance). 2 NUMA nodes. STREAM Triad: 42.9 GB/s single-node, 27.8 cross-QPI, 85.7 dual-socket first-touch. The GPU alone has ~11x the bandwidth of the whole 28-core complex.
specs.cpu_note: Broadwell-EP, AVX2+FMA, NO AVX-512/VNNI. Both sockets populated (28c/56t). GPU sits on CPU2's root complex = NUMA node 1, so GPU-feeding work wants 'numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1' - the OPPOSITE of the --interleave=all advice that suits CPU-only MoE runs on this same box.
